232005.note: Replaced the roads in the south: the loop past 019 to 038, with its east arm now on the visible gravel beside 029 to 037, the spur to 026 and 027, and the highway past it are traced from the photo. The north loops (001 to 018) are under canopy and kept from the source, and all 40 sites are within 40 m of a road.

232126.note: The lidar relief shows all five loops plainly as graded lanes, each with short pull-ins branching to the pads, and the listed sites sit at the ends of those pull-ins (001 to 009 north of loop A, 025 to 045 round loop B, 092 to 120 round loop E). OpenStreetMap's loops ran along the lanes' outer edges and are moved onto their middles (2 to 5 m); every site is within 40 m of a drawn road. Loops C and D carry no listed sites; the pull-ins aren't drawn.

232128.note: Split listing, shown as 2 areas that match the photo: the west loop (004 to 024) and the northeast loop (025 to 051) follow the visible lanes and their sites line them. 001 to 003 and one more have no point, and the group sites UGA and LGA sit off any drawn lane.

232140.note: The lidar intensity shows the loop and the entrance lane as a mid-gray gravel band under the trees, and the relief shows the same as a smooth graded strip; OpenStreetMap's loop sits on it within about 3 to 4 m, with the open grass lot inside its south end matching the photo. Every site is within 40 m of a drawn road (007 to 015, 019 and 020 sit 20 to 40 m off the loop, with no pull-ins showing). Nothing traced.

232174.note: The lidar intensity shows the campground loop as a plain asphalt band under the canopy and the relief shows its pull-ins to the pads (by 006, 011, 015, 016, 018 to 021); OpenStreetMap's loop and roads sit on the bands within about 3 m. Every site is within 40 m of a drawn road; the pull-ins aren't drawn. Nothing traced.

232175.note: Replaced: the lidar intensity shows the loop as a plain dark band under the trees (the relief confirms it as a graded lane), and the Forest Service line ran 5 to 10 m inside it along the south side past 013 and 012; redrawn on the band. Every site is within 40 m of a drawn road; 010 sits in a clearing just south of the loop and 004, 005 and 007 on pads off it, with no pull-ins drawn.

232176.note: Unchanged. The loop and the lane west of it follow the visible gravel through the autumn canopy, and all 14 sites are within 40 m of a drawn road; the spurs to 001, 003, 007, 010 and 022 are hidden by leaves, so nothing was traced.

232177.note: The lidar intensity shows the loop and the entrance lane as a continuous gray gravel band under the trees, and the relief as a smooth graded strip with the pull-ins to the pads branching off; OpenStreetMap's lines follow it within about 2 to 4 m (on the band's outer edge on the north and west). Every site is within 40 m of a drawn road; the pull-ins aren't drawn. Nothing traced.

232178.note: The lidar intensity shows the two loops, the lanes between them and Lincoln Road as darker bands among the mottled litter, and OpenStreetMap's lines follow them within about 2 to 4 m (the relief shows only Lincoln Road plainly). Every site is within 40 m of a drawn road; the pull-ins to 001 to 008 and 043 to 050 don't show. Nothing traced.

232179.note: Unchanged. All 25 points sit on a sewage treatment pond, its banks, a construction yard and beside condominiums; nothing within the frame is a campground or a campsite pad, so there is nowhere on the photo to move them to and the points are wrong.

232308.note: The gravel loop is drawn on the visible road, and A to D, F, H and J to L sit in the clearings beside it; E, G and I sit just inside the trees between the two arms.

232393.note: The lidar relief shows the loop past 001 to 016 and 021 to 028 as a crowned bank with ditches, and the Forest Service line sits on it within a few meters; traced the lane east from the loop by 016 to 017 and 020, which shows as the same bank and as a dark band in the intensity. Only 019 is more than 40 m from a drawn road; the way on to 018 and 019 shows only as a narrow path.

232394.note: Unchanged. The loop follows the visible lane and all 11 sites are within 40 m of it; zoomed on a 5 m grid, 008 and 009 sit in a shaded opening west of the loop where no lane shows plainly, so nothing was traced.

233476.note: The lidar intensity is mottled under the trees (2016 survey, 1.9 ground points per square meter) with no lane band, and the relief shows only a faint edge along the east side of the drawn loop by 03 to 07 and the levelled square by 05, so neither the loop's west side past 19 to 22 nor any spur to 08 to 11 can be checked against a plain band. Nothing traced.

233519.note: The paved lane past the shelter is now traced from the photo, continuing the drawn road from the junction north-west past IHC, which sits on the lawn beside it. The second, unnamed point sits on the open lawn east of the junction, with nothing on the photo marking a site there.

233573.note: Unchanged. The north loops, the long lane south and the south loop follow the visible lanes, and all 124 sites are within 40 m of a drawn road. Zoomed on a 5 m grid, the ground between the two north arms (064 to 068, 075 to 078) shows pads and short drives rather than a continuous lane, so nothing was traced.

233644.note: Split listing, shown as 3 areas that match the photo's clusters along the peninsula (01 to 08, 09 to 18, 19 to 64). The north and middle sites line the drawn road; at the south end the drawn roads run around the loops while 29 to 50 sit on paved lanes inside them that are only partly drawn.

233652.note: Split listing, shown as 2 areas. The main area's lanes past 01 to 55 and 57 to 86 are drawn, but the lettered sites A to X have no drawn lane, and Loop P (P01 to P16, across the bay) has no road at all (median 93 m away).

233676.note: The main road, the north road and the loops at both ends sit on the bands the lidar intensity shows and on the visible gravel; the main road is moved onto the middle of the gravel where it opens past the field (it ran along the north edge, about 3 m off), and the gravel lane south-west off it past S50 toward S51 and S52 is added, plain on the photo and continuing as a dark band into the trees. 9 of 111 sites are still more than 40 m from a drawn road (S47 to S49, S56, L53, L54, S41, N33, N34), where no lane shows plainly.

234674.note: Loops A, B and C and the D parking loop follow the visible pavement, but D04 to D99 west of the D loop are walk-in tent sites under full canopy, 40 to 160 m from the loop with footpaths only; 63 of 178 sites, about a third, are more than 40 m from any drawn road.

234714.note: Traced the paved road northwest from the circle, the lane north to E17 to E20, and the sandy lanes to the B and A group sites; checked over the photo after the rebuild. The D sites still have no drawn lane (the opening toward them is too faint to place).

234715.note: H1 to H7 sit on the visible tent pads on the lawn, and the drawn roads follow the visible pavement to the parking and the lane east.

239417.note: The lidar relief shows the loop past 13 to 19 and the lanes to 1 to 9 as crowned strips that OpenStreetMap's lines follow, but no lane runs east to 21 to 28: the only feature there is a narrow raised grade with a ditch running north-west to south-east past 25 to 28, which reads as an old railroad or logging grade, not a campground lane. 9 of 27 sites (10, 11, 22 to 28) stay more than 40 m from a drawn road. Nothing traced.

246520.note: Walk-in sites along the lakeshore: the lidar relief shows the drawn road along the ridge and, west of it, only narrow footpaths (a pair branching past 4 to 8 and a curving one to 5) leading to the sites, with no vehicle lane; the intensity is mottled. 8 of 15 sites (1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15) stay 48 to 85 m from any drawn road. Nothing traced.

251575.note: Unchanged. AL2 to AL12 are spread along the riverbank in leafless woods; no pads, tracks or roads show anywhere in the frame (likely paddle-in or hike-in sites), so there is nothing to trace and the points can't be checked.

251609.note: The lidar intensity shows the loop and both entrance roads as plain asphalt bands under the canopy, and the relief shows the pull-ins to the pads (by 01 to 03, 08 to 10, 14 and 15); the Forest Service lines sit on the bands within about 2 m. Every site is within 40 m of a drawn road; the pull-ins aren't drawn. Nothing traced.

251833.note: Loops A and B and the main road follow the visible pavement and their sites line them. G1, G2 and the walk-in sites H01 to H09 sit in the woods southeast with no drawn lane or path.

251946.note: The main road and the lane east follow the visible roads; the gravel drive to 201 and the lane west to the lot by 207 are now traced from the photo. 201 to 212 sit on pads along the open lawn west of the main road, which has no lane of its own, and 221 to 225 sit in the woods inside Spillway Road, which runs under full canopy (the lidar relief puts its bench 5 to 10 m east of the drawn line, so it's unconfirmed).

251963.note: A boat-to-shore campground on a mown point: the gravel lane south from the parking past 17 and 13 is traced from the photo, but 22 of 50 sites at the north end sit 40 to 125 m from it across open lawn with no vehicle lane.

255204.note: The loop around the field and the lane west follow the visible pavement, and 001 to 046 sit on the pads along them.

256347.note: Unchanged. The loop follows the visible gravel (its north end runs about 4 m south of the lane) and the sites sit on pads beside it; all 19 sites are within 40 m. Zoomed on a 5 m grid, 006's pad sits in the trees north of the loop with no lane to it showing, so nothing was traced.

261792.note: The entrance road and the small loop follow the visible gravel, with 001 to 003 along the entrance and 004 to 007 around the loop's lawn.

264293.note: 01 to 05 sit on the five lean-to roofs showing through the spruce, reached on footpaths from the track that ends at 01; 03, 04 and 05 are 50 to 90 m from it, more than half the sites without a drawn road.

270967.note: Replaced: OpenStreetMap's straight-sided loops cut across the sites, and the lidar relief shows the real lanes plainly as smooth graded bands under the canopy (12 ground points per square meter). Redrawn on them: the entrance from Lost River Road (which the photo confirms at its open west end), the big loop south past 5 to 7, east past 8 and 9 and north past 12 and 17, round the north past 18 to 20 and down the diagonal past 21 to 24, and the cross lane past 13 to 15. Every site is within 40 m of a drawn road; the pull-ins to the pads aren't drawn.

272174.note: 001 to 022 and 044 line the drawn lanes by the river. The lidar relief shows the web of lanes past 023 to 043 as smooth curving strips between raised tree islands, but the survey is sparse (1.7 per m²), the intensity shows the strips only faintly, and smooth strips there can't be told from mown lawn, so the lanes' middles can't be placed within a few metres. The Kiski group site still sits 300 m away with no lane. Nothing traced.

273778.note: The lidar relief shows loops A to G and the campground roads as crowned bands under the hardwoods, and the Forest Service lines sit on them; the A loop lane ran along its band's east edge and is redrawn on its middle (the rest copied). Only F05 to F07 are more than 40 m from a drawn road: they and F04 and F08 sit west of the F spur with no lane showing, so they read as walk-in sites.

274471.note: Site #1 to Site #5 sit by small tent pads in the woods above the end of Valley View Road; #2 to #5 are 43 to 84 m from the road with no vehicle lane showing, four of five sites without a drawn road.

10040547.note: Along the north and east shore the lidar relief shows a narrow cut path about 10 m north of the drawn Census line past 1 to 8, but the intensity shows no lane band there at 4.3 ground points per square meter, so it reads as the shore trail to walk-in sites rather than a road; the drawn shore lines can't be confirmed as roads, and 17 sits alone 91 m south of any. Only the west end (12 to 16, the lot and Grout Pond Road) shows plainly. Nothing traced.

10122722.note: Unchanged. Zoomed on a 5 m grid, the campground lane shows only as a soft grey band 5 to 8 m wide through the leafless woods, and the lidar relief shows the pads by 3 to 9 and Cabin 1 but not the lane itself, so it can't be placed to 3 m; 29 of 30 sites are still over 40 m from a drawn road (only the two highways are drawn).

10300159.note: The lidar intensity shows the campground loop as a plain gravel band under the trees, and it is redrawn on it (OpenStreetMap's loop ran 4 to 7 m inside on the west and south sides), with the entrance road and the parking-lot spur by 11 copied. The east sites (1 to 21) sit on river terraces south of the lot with no lane showing in either layer, so they read as walk-in sites; 13 of 54 are more than 40 m from a drawn road.
